# Implementation omitted per source limitation [S1]

The claim describes a volume partitioning method that adaptively divides volumes into sub-volumes (boxes) by clustering voxels based on volume and transfer function properties to minimize invisible voxels in visible subsets. It details the separation of non-zero gradient voxels (gradient boxes) from uniform regions (uniform boxes), filling remaining spaces with 'other' boxes, and notes the trade-offs of increasing box numbers (overhead and replicated storage). It also explains that uniform boxes are inefficient for lit rendering due to zero-gradient voxels, which gradient boxes solve. Finally, it mentions the growth rule (maximize size while keeping cost below a threshold) and contrasts this with region growing. All these specific facts are explicitly stated in Source [S1].
supported

The evidence explicitly states that 'uniform boxes alone work well for unilluminated rendering but are inefficient for lit rendering because they include many zero-gradient voxels for lighting computation.' It further explains that the method separates voxels with non-zero gradient magnitude (gradient boxes) to avoid unnecessary lighting computations. This directly supports the claim that the method is used when lit rendering performance is critical and the volume has distinct surface (gradient) and interior (uniform) regions.
